title: Be Still
teaser: Stop. Sit. One verse. One prayer. The week has done its work. Today is for being with what arrived.
theme: Sabbath. Reception, not analysis. The whole posture of the day is to close the page and sit.

modules.heading: STOP. BE STILL.

scripture_anchor.text: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.

modules.invitation:
Today is small.

Close the app. Sit with this verse for the day. We will be here tomorrow.

There is nothing to read past this line. The week was loud with words. Today is for none of them. Whatever has arrived in you over the last six days needs room to settle, and silence is the room it settles in. Read the verse once. Read it again, slower. Then put the book down.

The verb at the center of the verse is be. Not do. Not earn. Not figure out. Be — as in, allow yourself to be acted upon. Be reconciled. Receive what someone else is doing on your behalf. The whole posture of the day is the open hand of Day 4, held all the way through to evening.

If today is hard — if sitting still feels strange, if your hand wants to reach for the next thing, if the silence feels louder than the words were — that is also fine. The body has been moving for years. It will take more than one Sunday to teach it to stop. Notice the impulse. Set it down. Try again. The work of the day is not to be still successfully. The work of the day is to keep returning, gently, to the verse and the breath when the mind drifts.

There is nothing on this page to finish.

The runner has reached the gate. The chariot is on the road. The robe is on the chair. You do not have to do anything with any of that today. You only have to be where you are, with the One whose appeal the verse names. Tomorrow the next thing will arrive. Today is for being.
modules.prayerText: Father, I have nothing to do today but be with You. Amen.
